subject: Chemistry
title: Jabir ibn Hayyan: Father of Chemistry
description: A micro-lesson that makes Jabir ibn Hayyan: Father of Chemistry usable.

hook.text: Jabir ibn Hayyan invented distillation, crystallization, and named dozens of chemicals still used today.

buildup.text: Working in 8th-century Iraq, Jabir wrote over 300 texts on chemistry, medicine, and philosophy.

discovery.text: He discovered hydrochloric acid, nitric acid, and aqua regia—the only liquid that can dissolve gold.

twist.text: He developed the alembic still—a device for distillation that chemists used for a thousand years after him.

climax.text: The word 'gibberish' may come from 'Jabir'—his writings were so coded that Europeans couldn't understand them.

punchline.text: Acids, distillation, crystallization. One man built chemistry's foundation.

quiz.question: What liquid did Jabir ibn Hayyan discover that can dissolve gold?
options: Aqua regia—a mix of hydrochloric and nitric acid

details.summary: Jabir ibn Hayyan, an 8th-century Islamic scholar, systematized alchemical knowledge and introduced rigorous experimental methodology including precise measurement and reproducibility..
details.whyItMatters: Jabir's emphasis on controlled experimentation and documented procedures moved alchemy toward systematic science. His techniques for producing mineral acids enabled chemical analysis impossible with earlier methods.
takeaways: Jabir introduced systematic experimentation and documentation to alchemy
He developed distillation, crystallization, and acid preparation methods
His work laid the experimental foundation for Islamic Golden Age chemistry

faq.question: What specific chemical advances did Jabir ibn Hayyan contribute?
faq.answer: Jabir is credited with developing processes for producing hydrochloric acid, nitric acid, and aqua regia. He refined distillation apparatus, described crystallization and filtration techniques, and classified substances into categories. His work described over two thousand chemical procedures.

faq.question: Why is there debate about which works were actually written by Jabir?
faq.answer: Over three thousand texts are attributed to Jabir, far more than one person could write. Scholars believe many were written by later authors under his name, a common practice in Islamic and medieval tradition. The Jabirian corpus represents a school of thought rather than a single author.
